contents.content:
Trekking lets you enjoy the outdoors, challenge yourself, and explore new places. You can find the best places for trekking near Bangalore. There are easy and scenic trails, and hard and rewarding climbs. You can choose what suits you best.

Key Takeaways

  • Nandi Hills, Savanadurga, Skandagiri, Anthargange, Ramanagara, and Kanakapura Hills are some of the best treks near Bangalore.
  • You can see old forts, temples, caves, waterfalls, lakes, and animals there. 
  • October to March is the best time to go. The weather is good and the place is green.
  • You need clothes, shoes, water, snacks, sunscreen, hat, first aid, medicines, torch, whistle, camera, and binoculars.
  • You must follow these rules: check the weather and trail, follow the guide, stay with the group, don’t litter or make noise, and respect the culture and animals.

Table of Contents

Nandi Hills is one of the most famous and accessible trekking destinations near Bangalore (64 Km). It is located at an altitude of 1478 m and offers a panoramic view of the surrounding hills and valleys. Nandi Hills is also known for its historical significance as the summer retreat of Tipu Sultan, the ruler of Mysore in the 18th century. There are many attractions and landmarks on the top of Nandi Hills, such as the Tipu’s Drop, the Nandi Temple, the Amrita Sarovar, and the Nehru Nilaya.

Difficulty level, distance, and duration

The trek to Nandi Hills is easy to moderate and suitable for beginners and families. The distance of the trek is about 4 km one way and the duration is about 2 hours. The trek starts from the base of the hill and follows a well-marked trail that passes through forests, gardens, and arches. The trek ends at the summit, where you can enjoy the sunrise and the views.

Tipu’s Drop: This is a place where Tipu Sultan threw his enemies down from a cliff. It is on the west side of Nandi Hills. You can also see the sunrise and sunset from here.

Nandi Temple: On the south side of the Nandi Hills stands an old temple dedicated to Nandi, the bull of Lord Shiva. At the entrance, a large statue of Nandi welcomes visitors. Made from a single rock, it's impressive in its size and simplicity.

Amrita Sarovar: Up north in Nandi Hills, find Amrita Sarovar, a lake with special springs that never run dry. Locals call it the "Lake of Nectar" because its water is clean and calm. Surrounded by green plants and colorful flowers, it's a wonderful spot to relax and enjoy the fresh breeze. Remember, it's a sacred place for the people there, so be respectful during your visit.

Nehru Nilaya: On the east side of Nandi Hills, find Nehru Nilaya, a colonial bungalow built during British rule. It used to be the home of Sir Mark Cubbon, the British commissioner of Mysore Mysore. Later, India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, loved spending his summers there. Today, you can stay at Nehru Nilaya or visit the museum inside to learn about its history!

Best time to visit and what to expect

Nandi Hills shines brightest between October and March. The weather is awesome, not too hot, not too cold, just right at 10°C to 25°C. See everything clearly, no fog hiding the view! Look out for eucalyptus, silver oak, and even coffee trees! Colorful wildflowers bloom everywhere. Spot friendly birds like mynas and parakeets, maybe even playful monkeys and mongoose!

Savanadurga is one of the largest monoliths in Asia and a challenging trekking destination near Bangalore(47.6 Km). It is located at an altitude of 1226 m and offers a stunning view of the surrounding hills and forests. Savanadurga is also known for its geological and historical importance as a part of the Deccan Plateau and a former fortress of Kempegowda and Tipu Sultan. 

Difficulty level, distance, and duration

To climb up Savanadurga Hill is a tough one, best for trekkers who are used to challenges and like exploring. It's not too long, about 6 kilometers there and back, but it takes around 4-5 hours to complete. Start at the bottom of a giant hill and follow a path that gets steeper and rockier as you go. There will be big rocks, smooth stones, and even narrow gaps to climb over. But all that effort is worth it when you reach the top! From there, you can soak in the amazing views and have some fun adventures.

Attractions and highlights

Savanadurga is a place of natural, historical, and religious importance. Some of the attractions and highlights that you can explore on the top of Savanadurga are:

Savandi Veerabhadreshwara Swamy and Narasimha Swamy temples: Upon a hill stand two ancient temples, side-by-side. One honors Lord Shiva, the other Lord Vishnu. Built in a simple yet beautiful style, these temples draw many followers who travel to visit them. Each year, the temples come alive with special celebrations, like Shivaratri for Lord Shiva and Narasimha Jayanti for Lord Vishnu, bringing together devotees to celebrate their faith.

Arkavathi river: Flowing alongside rolling hills, this branch of the Cauvery River offers a peaceful escape for nature lovers. The river snakes its way through the landscape, creating a scenic view for hikers. Imagine the gentle breeze carrying the chirping of birds as you admire the beauty around you. This hidden gem also invites you to explore its waters. 

Manchanabele dam: This dam is built across the Arkavathi river which serves two important purposes. First, it stores water to irrigate nearby fields and provide drinking water for villages. This helps keep the land healthy and people happy! Second, the dam is a popular spot for picnics and birdwatching. Bring your family for a day out - you might see pelicans soaring in the sky or herons fishing in the shallows. The dam is a valuable resource and a fun place to visit!

Best time to visit and what to expect

October to March is Savandurga's prime time. Cool, dry air makes exploring easy, with temperatures between 15°C and 25°C. Sunrises around 6:30 am bathe the rocky landscape in warm light. Expect rugged terrain and a majestic atmosphere. Keep your eyes peeled for monkeys, leopards, vultures, and eagles!

Skandagiri is a great spot for trekking near Bangalore, about 60.7 kilometers away. It's up high at 1450 meters. You can see amazing clouds and the sunrise from there. Skandagiri used to be a fort way back in the 1700s, during Tipu Sultan's rule in Mysore. You can still see parts of the old fort, like walls and gates, up on Skandagiri.

Difficulty level, distance, and duration

The hike to Skandagiri is somewhat challenging, about 8 kilometers round trip, taking 4 to 5 hours. Starting from Papagni Temple at the bottom of the hill, you'll go through forests, grasslands, and boulders. The trek ends at the summit, where you can enjoy a spectacular sunrise and views.

Attractions and highlights

Skandagiri is a place of historical, natural, and spiritual importance. Some of the attractions and highlights that you can explore on the top of Skandagiri are:

Papagni Temple: This temple is old and dedicated to Goddess Parvati, also called Papagni. It sits at the bottom of the hill and marks the beginning of the trek. People who worship Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati often visit this temple as a pilgrimage.

Ruins of the fort: The main attraction of Skandagiri is the remains of the hill fortress of Tipu Sultan, who battled against the British in the Anglo-Mysore wars.

Sunrise and clouds: This is the highlight of the trek, where you witness the sunrise behind the clouds, casting a magical glow over the sky and landscape. You can also see the clouds below you, giving you a feeling of being on top of the world.

Best time to visit and what to expect

The ideal time to visit Skandagiri is from November to January, when the weather is cool and dry, and visibility is good. Temperatures range from 15°C to 20°C, and sunrise occurs around 6:30 am. You can enjoy clear, colorful skies and a misty, green valley. Wildlife such as peacocks, eagles, and monkeys are often spotted during this time.

Anthargange is one of the most unique and exciting trekking destinations near Bangalore(66.7 Km). It is located at an altitude of 1712 m and offers a combination of trekking, caving, and rappelling. Anthargange is also known for its geological and religious significance as a volcanic formation of boulders and caves and a pilgrimage site for the devotees of Lord Shiva. There are many attractions and highlights on the top of Anthargange, such as the Anthargange Temple, the perennial spring, the various caves and rock formations, and the thrilling activities of cave exploration and rappelling.

Difficulty level, distance, and duration

The trek to Anthargange is moderate and suitable for adventurous and curious trekkers. The distance of the trek is about 4-6 km round trip and the duration is about 3 to 4 hours. The trek starts from the Anthargange Temple at the base of the hill and follows a steep and narrow trail that passes through forests, boulders, and caves. The trek ends at the summit, where you can enjoy the views and the activities.

Attractions and highlights

Anthargange is a place of natural, spiritual, and adventurous importance. Some of the attractions and highlights that you can explore on the top of Anthargange are:

Anthargange Temple: The Anthargange Temple, also known as Shri Dakshina Kashi Vishwanatha Swamy Temple, is an ancient shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva. Anthargange means the Ganges from the deep. Located at the hill's base, it marks the starting point of the trek. The temple is renowned for its perennial spring, emerging from a small opening in the rocks, considered sacred by locals.

Caves and rock formations: Anthargange's caves and rock formations are the big draw here. The caves and rock formations show how volcanoes formed the hill. They display many differently shaped rocks and caves. You can check out many caves and rocks, including some mysterious volcanic ones. You can also try caving and rappelling, safe adventures for hikers.

Views and activities: The best part of the trek is the views and activities. You can see hills and valleys all around and do fun stuff. Watch the sunrise and sunset, look at birds and stars, and camp with friends and family around a bonfire.

Best time to visit and what to expect

The ideal time to visit Anthargange is from October to March. The weather is cool and dry, and visibility is good. Temperatures range from 15°C to 25°C and sunrise is around 6:30 am. You'll encounter rocky, rugged terrain and a mysterious atmosphere. Wildlife like bats, owls, bears, and leopards can be spotted.

Ramanagara is a famous trekking spot near Bangalore! just 46.7 kilometers away. It's 747 meters high. It has lots of fun things to do for trekkers. Ramanagara is special! because it was where they filmed the famous movie Sholay. People also know it for making silk and watching birds.
On top of Ramanagara, there are cool places to visit! like Ramadevara Betta, Pattabhi Rama Temple, Kanva, and Janapada Loka reservoirs. Plus, you can go rock climbing and camping there too.

Difficulty level, distance, and duration

The trek to Ramanagara is perfect for everyone! It's about 6 kilometers round trip and takes 3 to 4 hours. You start at the bottom of the hill and follow a clear path through forests, fields and rocks. The trek ends at the top, where you can enjoy the views and activities.

Attractions and highlights

Ramanagara is a place of cultural, natural, and adventurous importance. Some of the attractions and highlights that you can explore on the top of Ramanagara are:

Ramadevara Betta: Ramadevara Betta is the top spot in Ramanagara. It's where they filmed the famous movie Sholay. You can explore the rocky area and caves seen in the movie. Plus, there are statues of the characters and director on the hill.

Pattabhi Rama Temple: Pattabhi Rama Temple is an old temple honoring Lord Rama. It's on the east side of the hill! and has stunning architecture and sculptures. People who worship Lord Rama come here for festivals like Ram Navami and Hanuman Jayanti.

Kanva and Janapada Loka reservoirs: Kanva and Janapada Loka reservoirs are man-made lakes near the hill. They offer a peaceful setting! with views of the hills and sky reflected in the water. You can relax in the breeze and watch the birds. Nearby, Janapada Loka is a museum displaying Karnataka's folk art and culture.

Rock climbing and camping: Rock climbing and camping are fun things to do at the top of Ramanagara. It has lots of rocks and boulders! perfect for climbing and rappelling. You can also camp there and enjoy the night sky and a bonfire with your friends and family.

Best time to visit and what to expect

The ideal time to visit Ramanagara is from October to March. The weather is nice! and the scenery is lush green. Temperatures range from 15°C to 25°C! and you can catch a beautiful sunrise around 6:30 am. You'll encounter rocky terrain and a lively atmosphere. Keep an eye out for wildlife like vultures, kites, peacocks, and bears.

Kanakapura Hills is a calm trekking spot near Bangalore! just 75 kilometers away. It's 1075 meters high and surrounded by lush greenery. People love it for its natural beauty and spiritual vibes. It's part of the Bananthimari forest range and home to the Art of Living Foundation.

Difficulty level, distance, and duration

The trek to Kanakapura Hills is easy and perfect for nature lovers and families. It's about 5 kilometers round trip and takes 2 to 3 hours. You start at the Bananthimari Temple at the base of the hill! and follow a gentle and scenic trail through forests, fields and streams. The trek ends at the summit, where you can enjoy the views and activities.

Attractions and highlights

Kanakapura Hills is a place of natural, religious, and ecological importance. Some of the attractions and highlights that you can explore on the top of Kanakapura Hills are:

Bananthimari Temple: Bananthimari Temple is an old temple dedicated to Goddess Bananthimari, also known as the Mother of the Forest. It's at the base of the hill and marks the beginning of the trek. People who worship Goddess Bananthimari visit here for festivals like Navratri and Ugadi.

Kabbalamma Temple: This ancient temple honors Goddess Bananthimari, also known as the Mother of the Forest. It sits at the base of the hill and marks the beginning of the trek. People who worship Goddess Bananthimari come here for festivals like Navratri and Ugadi.

Hosadoddi Lake: Hosadoddi Lake is a lovely spot close to the hills, offering a peaceful setting for hikers. The water mirrors the hills and sky, and you can feel the gentle breeze while watching the birds.

Mekedatu-Chunchi Falls: This beautiful waterfall sits close to the hill and offers a breathtaking view for hikers. You'll witness water rushing down a narrow gorge! forming a misty rainbow. And you can hear the powerful sound of the water as it flows. 

Wildlife and birds: The trek gets really exciting! when you see all the different animals and birds along the way and on the hilltop. You'll notice elephants, deer, monkeys, and even leopards. And keep an eye out for kingfishers, parrots, hornbills, and peacocks flying around too.

Best time to visit and what to expect

The best time to visit Kanakapura Hills is from October to March, when the weather is pleasant and the scenery is green. The temperature ranges from 15°C to 25°C, and the sunrise is around 6:30 a.m. You can expect to see lush and green terrain and a calm and peaceful atmosphere. However, sometimes there might be heavy rainfall during these months, so it's good to carry an umbrella just in case. Also, keep in mind that sunrises can vary depending on the exact location within the hills.

Things to carry and safety measures

The things to carry for trekking to Nandi Hills include:

  • Comfortable clothes and shoes
  • Water and snacks
  • Sunscreen and hat
  • First aid kit and medicines
  • Torch and whistle
  • Camera and binoculars

The safety measures to follow while trekking to Nandi Hills include:

  • Check the weather and trail conditions before starting the trek
  • Follow the guide and instructions and do not wander off the trail
  • Stay with the group and do not lag behind or go ahead
  • Avoid littering and noise and respect the environment
  • Do not feed or disturb the wildlife and keep a safe distance
  • Do not venture near the edge of the cliff, lake or the waterfall
